intro: Lesson 93: Writing and performing a volcano poem. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Volcano words
points: similes: like angry bees, slow as honey

parts.text: Line 1 (sound): Boom! The mountain clears its throat.
Line 2 (sight): Grey ash rises like a giant's breath.
Line 3 (action): Molten rivers crawl and hiss,
Line 4 (feeling): and the valley holds its breath.

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: A four-line stanza with sound, sight, simile and personification

panels.title: Read it aloud
points: Ask a partner for one suggestion
Change one word to make it stronger

keywords.def: a group of lines in a poem
a word that sounds like its meaning
a comparison using like or as
change writing to make it better

questions.q: Make a line with a sound word and a precise verb
questions.a: For example: Hiss! The lava creeps.

questions.q: Core: write a four-line stanza with a sound, a sight, a simile and personification
questions.a: A stanza with the four features

questions.q: Extend: write a second stanza about the volcano calming down
Stretch: read your poem aloud and make one change from a partner's suggestion
Which line is the most powerful?
questions.a: C) Molten rivers crawl and hiss.. It has a precise verb (crawl), onomatopoeia (hiss) and personification.
